rationale: Bounded injectivity proof: forall distinct String values within bounded length, the byte sequences fed to blake3 Hasher differ. Risk is invariant violation on a bounded data type.
Bounded injectivity proof: forall distinct i64 values, i.to_le_bytes() produces distinct [u8; 8] — known true by i64 LE bijection, but Kani provides independent verification.
Kani harness proves that String and Integer variants produce different byte sequences (length + content) for all bounded values, preventing accidental hash collisions.
Statistical determinism proof: generate WorkflowSource, call canonical_digest twice, assert equality across many trials.
Defense-in-depth: statistical verification across larger input space than Kani can bound. Complements Kani injectivity proof.
Proptest verifies that step reordering changes the digest through ordered step ID hashing in canonical_digest().

contract_clause: Finish value changes compiled workflow digest
rationale: End-to-end: parse → compile_source → verify compiled_workflow.digest() matches source change. Closes GAP-2 and GAP-6.
Integration test verifying that renaming the finish step ID changes the compiled workflow digest. Closes GAP-3.

contract_clause: Finish result type (String vs Integer) changes digest
rationale: Integration test: compile workflow with String finish, then with Integer finish at same value, verify different digests. Closes GAP-4.
Equivalence test: canonical_digest() from both paths produce identical output for same input. Mitigates HAZ-1 duplicate code divergence risk.
Compile-time assertion that all current ScalarValue variants are explicitly matched (unreachable _ arm). Mitigates HAZ-2.
Audit that digest path has no unsafe, no time/random/IO, no runtime field inclusion.
Structural guarantee: canonical_digest takes &WorkflowSource not &CompiledWorkflow, but proptest defense-in-depth validates IR layout changes do not affect digest.

Digest computation is a pure, stateless function. The digest lifecycle (parsed→digest→lowered→validated→persisted) is purely sequential with no concurrent interleavings, no retry loops, no distributed protocols. TLA+ applies to temporal/state-machine properties with interleavings.
evidence_of_non_applicability: boundary-map.md confirms no concurrency, no async, no IO in digest subsystem. workflow-model.md describes linear sequential pipeline with idempotent pure function at core. No temporal hazards requiring state-machine model checking.

rationale: Verus is designed for proving Rust-local invariants on pure/core functions with Verus-compatible data structures. The digest properties here are behavioral (different inputs → different outputs) rather than type-level invariants. The core dependency blake3::Hasher is external and not Verus-verified. Proving hash properties through Verus would require ghost modeling of blake3 internals which is disproportionate for P1 scope.
evidence_of_non_applicability: digest_step_primitive uses blake3::Hasher (external crate, not Verus-compatible). Proof seeds recommend kani/proptest/integration-test as primary layers. No safety-critical invariant expressed as Verus refinement.

rationale: Flux refinements apply to data-level numeric/index predicates (e.g., 'this index is within bounds', 'this value is non-zero'). The properties here are function-level (injectivity, determinism, variant discrimination) that are better expressed as Kani harnesses or proptest properties. The existing types (ScalarValue, WorkflowDigest) are already well-typed; no refinement annotations would add value.
evidence_of_non_applicability: type-contracts.md confirms types prevent illegal states (ScalarValue enum, WorkflowDigest [u8; 32] repr(transparent)). No data refinements needed on top of existing Rust type system.

rationale: Digest subsystem has zero concurrency: no threads, no async, no channels, no atomics, no locks. canonical_digest is a pure synchronous function.
evidence_of_non_applicability: boundary-map.md confirms: no threads, no async, no channels, no atomics. boundary-map.md Async Boundary section: 'Digest computation is synchronous. Compilation is synchronous. All relevant functions return Result<T, E>, not Future<T>.'

rationale: Digest subsystem has zero unsafe code. Both vb_compile and vb_core have #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. No raw pointers, no FFI, no interior mutability UB risk.
evidence_of_non_applicability: boundary-map.md Unsafe Boundary section: 'No unsafe blocks exist in any digest-relevant code path.' compile/mod.rs line 1: '#![forbid(unsafe_code)]'. vb_core/src/workflow/mod.rs line 1: '#![forbid(unsafe_code)]'.

rationale: Digest function operates on typed AST (WorkflowSource, StepPrimitive, ScalarValue), not raw bytes. Fuzzing raw bytes into the digest would require going through the parser (out of scope for this bead). The typed API is better exercised via proptest (generates valid typed values) and Kani (exhaustively explores bounded type domains).
evidence_of_non_applicability: boundary-map.md Parser Boundary section: 'The digest function accepts a typed AST, never raw bytes.' Fuzzing the parser boundary is a separate concern (YAML parsing robustness) not in this bead's scope.
